english.html: ad that Nicomedes, King of Bithynia, after the death of Ariarathes, King of Cappadocia, invaded his kingdom, and promised marriage to Laodice, widow of the said Ariarathes; whereat Mithridates, brother of Laodice, being angered, drove Nicomedes out of Cappadocia, and restored it to another Ariarathes, son of Laodice: whom nevertheless he afterwards had killed by one named Gordius; whereupon Nicomedes, fearing that Mithridates, having made himself stronger by the accession of Cappadocia, might afterwards invade Bithynia, suborned a young man of very good grace to present himself to the Roman people as another son of Ariarathes, and to ask of them the kingdom of Cappadocia: and so that the thing might be made more probable, sent with him Laodice his wife (who also, as we have said above, had formerly been married to the first Ariarathes) to testify that this was her child, and that of Ariarathes her first husband: but to prevent his desire from producing its effect, Mithridates sent the above-named Gordius (who by Mithridates' command had killed the first Ariarathes) to assure the Roman people of the contrary: who, having discovered the fraud and rashness of the one and the other, only deprived Mithridates of Cappadocia and Nicomedes of Paphlagonia, and gave liberty to both peoples. Nevertheless the Cappadocians refused it, saying it was not possible for any people to live without a King. Whereupon the Senate constituted Ariobarzanes their King <sup class="mk" data-key="q">q</sup>. A Jew of Sidon resembled so well in body, face, speech and bearing Alexander, son of Herod Antipas, king of the Jews (whom the father had had killed), that he gave several to understand that he was Alexander, son of Herod, giving several tokens of Alexander, and of the private matters of the house of Herod, instructed by someone who was lending him a hand. And the better to colour the imposture, he said that the soldiers who had taken charge to kill him had given him a way to save himself, and had killed another in his place: in which he knew so well how to practise, and to impose upon the greater part of the Jews, that they followed him as king, and he came to Rome in royal

notes.citation: Justin, Epitome of the Philippic History of Pompeius Trogus, book 38, chapters 1–2 (the print's xxxij for xxxviij)
notes.original: Iuſtin. au xxxij. liure de l'hiſtoire de Trogue Pompee.
notes.gloss: Nicomedes III of Bithynia and Mithridates VI contend for Cappadocia; the suborned pretender and the senate's grant of liberty, refused by the Cappadocians, who received Ariobarzanes as king.

lines: ſons que Nicomedes Roy de Bithynie, apres la mort
d'Ariarathes Roy de Cappadoce, inuada ſon royaume,
& promit mariage à Laodice, vefue dudit Ariarathes.
de quoy irrité Mithridates, frere de Laodice, chaſſa
Nicomedes de Cappadoce, & le rendit a vn autre Aria-
rathes, fils de Laodice: lequel toutesfois il fit apres tuer
par vn nommé Gordius, dont Nicomedes craignãt que
Mithridates, ſ'eſtant rendu plus fort, par l'acceſſion de
Cappadoce, n'inuadaſt apres la Bithynie, ſuborne vn
ieune homme de fort bonne grace, pour ſe preſenter
comme vn autre fils d'Ariarathes au peuple Romain,
& luy demander le royaume de Cappadoce: & à fin
que la choſe ſe rendit plus vray ſemblable, enuoya a-
uec luy Laodice ſa femme (laquelle auſſi, comme
auons dit deſſus, auoit eſté mariée iadis, au premier A-
riarathes) pour teſmoigner, que c'eſtoit ſon enfant, &
d'Ariarathes ſon premier mari: mais pour empeſcher,
que ſon deſir ne produiſiſt ſon effect, Mithridates en-
uoya le ſuſnommé Gordius, qui (par le commandemẽt
de Mithridates auoit tué le premier Ariarathes) pour
aſſeurer le contraire au peuple Romain: lequel ayant
deſcouuert la fraude, & temerité de l'vn & de l'autre,
priua ſeulement Mithridates de la Cappadocie,
& Nicomedes de la Paphlagonie, & donna liber-
té à tous les deux peuples. Toutesfois les Cappa-
dociens la reffuſerent, diſant n'eſtre poſſible, qu'au-
cun peuple viue ſans Roy. Dont le Senat luy con-
ſtitua Roy Ariobarzanes {q}. Vn Iuif de Sidoine, re-
ſembloit ſi bien de corps, de viſage, de parole, & de
contenances Alexandre fils d'Herode Antipas, roy des
Iuifz (que le pere auoit fait tuer) qu'il fit entendre à
pluſieurs qu'il eſtoit Alexandre, fils d'Herode. don-
nant pluſieurs enſeignes d'Alexandre, & des choſes pri-
uées de la maiſon d'Herode, inſtruit de quelqu'vn qui
luy tenoit la main. Et pour mieux colorer l'impo-
ſture, diſoit que les ſoldats qui auoyent prins charge
de le tuer, luy donnerent chemin pour ſe ſauuer, & en
tuerent vn autre en ſa place: en quoy il ſceut ſi bien
pratiquer, & impoſer à la pluſpart des Iuifz, qu'ils le
ſuyuoient comme roy, & ſ'en vint à Rome en apparat
Iuſtin. au
xxxij. liure
de l'hiſtoire
de Trogue
Pompee.
